review_type: Independent visual review of all ten supplied browser screenshots
score_scale: 0–10; judged within the supplied low-resolution, low-poly visual style
verdict: The visible scene satisfies the core brief. The furnished room now reads as an occupied apartment within a grounded, multi-storey urban building. No required visual fix is demonstrated by these screenshots. Remaining weaknesses are optional presentation and architectural polish.

observations: The dense kitchen, dining furniture, utensils, bed and plants preserve a furnished, lived-in room.
The yellow fridge presents solid opaque faces; the wall and floor do not show through it.
The foreground plant pot is solid, with visible soil and distinct leaf silhouettes rather than rectangular image cards.
The distant bedroom window is filled by the neighbouring facade, supporting the apartment setting.
The entrance is surrounded by continuous opaque wall, with no entrance-side window visible.
The pot is opaque, and the plant retains cutout leaf edges.
The TV, table and cabinet maintain the original domestic character.
Opposing and repeated doors clearly communicate a shared corridor and neighbouring flats.
The tight width, bare bulbs and rough textures form a coherent worn apartment corridor.
The requested rough corridor texture treatment should be retained.
The distant stair access is visually subdued, but this is not a demonstrated functional obstruction.
The close brick facade almost completely fills the opening and produces the requested claustrophobia.
Both AC units sit on visible supports in wall space between windows; neither overlays a window opening.
Window recesses, floor bands and cast shadows give the opposing facade useful depth at this style level.
The bed and curtains frame a close opposing building, making the bedroom feel enclosed by the city.
AC units have visible brackets and clear separation from neighbouring window openings.
The facade has coherent storeys and a vertical pipe; no floating attachment is evident.
The occupied building visibly reaches the pavement and has multiple storeys, a street entrance and a canopy.
The narrow gap to the adjacent brick building supports the confined interior views.
The small, varied openings on the occupied floor are confirmed as actual windows by image 09, not escaped furniture.
The street and pavement terminate abruptly against the flat background at the far right, limiting this wide establishing view.
No stair half-landing is visibly protruding through the street facade.
The close balconies make the courtyard relationship particularly convincing from inside the apartment.
Balcony slabs meet the wall beneath doors, with side enclosures and diagonal supports.
The visible AC unit occupies clear wall space rather than blocking the adjacent window.
Tall close walls, continuous ground, bins, litter and pipes establish a grounded service courtyard.
The balcony braces visibly connect slabs to the facade.
Windows remain readable and clear of the visible AC units.
Some surface repetition is apparent, but it is compatible with the intended low-resolution style.
A stair flight, handrails, a turning area and an overhead return flight establish a real stairwell.
The small visible window is surrounded by wall and is not visibly bisected by a landing slab.
The close crop, similar dark tones and chunky overhead stair geometry make the circulation harder to read than the rest of the scene.
This image does not establish full-route clearance or walkability.
All three differently sized original windows are visibly embedded in the occupied facade, with sills.
Curtains, the TV and table, and kitchen fixtures appear behind the openings; they do not read as props escaped onto the exterior.
The opposing balcony doors, slabs, rails and braces have a coherent attachment relationship.

The occupied floor has a noticeably different wall texture and irregular opening rhythm compared with the repeated floors above and below; this is an integration polish issue, not a failure to enclose the apartment.

brief_assessment.furnished_original_room: The supplied interior views show a coherent furnished room. Exact asset-by-asset preservation cannot be established without an earlier reference.
brief_assessment.grounded_multi_storey_apartment: Pass in the visible evidence, especially images 05, 07 and 09.
brief_assessment.entrance_side_windows_removed: Pass for the entrance wall shown in image 01.
brief_assessment.shared_corridor_and_neighbours: Pass visually in image 02. Interior layouts behind neighbouring doors are not visible.
brief_assessment.ac_and_balcony_attachment: Pass for visible attachments and window clearance in images 03, 04, 06, 07 and 09.
brief_assessment.rough_corridor_textures: Appropriate and retained; no cleanup recommended.
brief_assessment.plant_pot_opacity_and_leaf_cutouts: Pass for the visible plants in images 00 and 01.
brief_assessment.stair_facade_and_window_corrections: The exterior shows no visible landing extrusion, and the visible stairwell window is clear of a crossing slab. Complete geometry clearance is not provable from these views.
brief_assessment.window_sills: Clearly visible on the occupied exterior openings in image 09.

strengths: Interior window views convincingly place the room in a narrow urban gap.
The room retains its furniture density and domestic identity.
The shared corridor and grounded exterior communicate an apartment building rather than a detached trailer.
AC units and balconies have readable supports and occupy plausible facade locations.
The requested opaque fridge and pots, plus cutout plant leaves, look correct in the supplied views.

prioritized_remaining_issues.issue: The stairwell is the least visually legible part of the review.
image_evidence: 08-stair-landing.png: the overhead stepped underside dominates the top half, while similar wall and stair values obscure the turning area.
prioritized_remaining_issues.minimal_fix: If this is a regular player view, use a small existing-light adjustment to distinguish the landing and treads. Preserve the rough textures; do not rebuild the stairs solely on this screenshot.
prioritized_remaining_issues.confidence: High for visual readability; insufficient evidence to assert a circulation or collision defect.

prioritized_remaining_issues.issue: The occupied storey reads as a visually separate facade band.
image_evidence: 09-occupied-exterior.png: its flatter grey-brown wall texture and three irregular window sizes stand apart from the yellow repeated storeys.
05-building-context.png: the occupied openings are visibly distinct in the wider composition.
prioritized_remaining_issues.minimal_fix: If exterior consistency matters, match the occupied wall texture tint or scale more closely to the adjacent storeys. Preserve the three original windows and their sizes.
prioritized_remaining_issues.confidence: High; the difference is visible, but can reasonably read as a renovated storey.

prioritized_remaining_issues.issue: The wide exterior exposes an abrupt end to the surrounding world.
image_evidence: 05-building-context.png: the far-right pavement and street edge meet the plain grey background.
prioritized_remaining_issues.minimal_fix: Only if this wide angle is player-accessible or used for presentation, extend the existing street surface or hide its end behind an existing building mass.
prioritized_remaining_issues.confidence: High for this screenshot; player visibility is unknown.

limitations: All ten named screenshots were opened with view_image and inspected.
No browser session, implementation edits, source-geometry audit or additional agents were used.
Static images cannot verify collision, full stair traversal, hidden neighbouring rooms, material behavior at every angle, animation or runtime performance.
No earlier screenshot set was used as proof of asset preservation or claimed corrections.
